Continue to a round 3 verify of SC-007 alone, or accept the spec as its verdict? (REVIEW=spec: an accept stands as the spec review's verdict)

Round 2 raised one new item, that FR-010 had no criterion and could not have been raised before FR-010 existed. SC-007 answers it almost word for word in the clauses the reviewer itself proposed (one extension module, every STAGES entry a Python function with its docstring, no #[cfg(test)] mod tests outside the test files). No packing is involved: the only numbers are the 40 and 80 household roll sizes and section 7's Rust line caps, which are copied from the design, and nothing is being fitted to them.
what: The spec stands as it reads now, and this accept is the spec review's verdict. The session records it in the spec's Review history as round 3, closed by the arbiter's accept, then goes on to plan. Two things are left, and neither blocks the spec. First, SC-007 inherits FR-010's condition ('if the decision is Rust') and should be read as applying only then; a plan task can say so. Round 1's aside about step 0's bookkeeping (closing 427 and 435, moving 435's T05/T07/T09 to 405) is the session's to carry out and track as a task. It is not a spec gap.

asked: Third rounds of the work-budget check on three water stages, paper derivations with no engine change. water_frame: round 1 UNDERIVED (pins unsourced; slack named work), round 2 UNDERIVED (the contract did not declare the three settlement flags it writes) - now declared. field: round 1 UNDERIVED (an invented texture factor), round 2 LOOSE with an exact correction (slack 1, the bends a run term) - applied as stated, the outline's worst cell measured. sink: round 1 UNDERIVED (a sampled rim), round 2 UNDERIVED (pond_seat uncited, arithmetic slips, the band too narrow) - corrected, the side step's reach labeled a GUESS. Each round's findings were new and each was fixed as ruled. Continue to round 3 on all three?
why: The six verdicts converge with no reversals and no oscillation: each round 2 finding is NEW and narrower than round 1 (field is down to one factor with an exact correction, water_frame to an undeclared Writes line, sink to one uncited reach and some arithmetic), and each was fixed as stated. A round costs about four minutes of agent time (19:52 to 19:56 in the cascade). Accepting would leave three stages without the SOUND verdict that SC-001 and the GM's adversarial standard require, for no saving worth having. There is no packing here: these are paper operation counts, and the GUESS figures (the pond's set-back limit and its sway across the fall) are inputs to the contract that the count takes as given, not ground anyone is defending.
what: Run round 3 of the work-budget agent, MODE BUDGET, on all three bundles, rebuilt from the corrected derivations. water_frame: check that the three settlement flags and the archetype test now in the contract's Reads and Writes give the 4-op factor its reason, and that nothing else the stage writes is still undeclared. field: check that slack 1 and the bend run term (4 x 3 x 2 x 12 = 288 at 20, growing as the fan's side) are applied as round 2 stated, along with the measured worst outline cell and the brook substitution. sink: check that the lines-solved count and the offset are derived from the side step's reach that pond_seat states (labeled GUESS), and that the 6a band, the crop edge across the band, and the dike, forbidden-ground and gather-cell factors are counted. Round 3 judges whether the count follows from the stated reach, not whether the reach is researched, which is the claims round's job. Pin the budget for any stage ruled SOUND. If a stage gets LOOSE with an exact tighter bound, apply it and pin it without a round 4. If any stage gets a fourth UNDERIVED, or a finding that undoes an earlier fix, bring it back here with the verdicts before spending another round.

asked: Under the continue on ask:444-T02-water-round-3, field and sink have each had a fourth UNDERIVED from the work-budget agent, which that ruling sends back here. Each round's findings were new and narrower, and each was fixed as stated; the fourth rounds found real defects again - field: no step selects the outline's plots, and 188 does not follow from its reason (about 367 by the derivation's own rule); sink: a binary search on a closed outline, the ditch tested once rather than per line, and the setback's intervals unswept. pond_bank has a second UNDERIVED (cell sizes and densest-case bounds missing). Rounds cost about 2 minutes of agent time each plus the session's rewrite. Continue to a fifth round on field and sink, or another course - and is there a question here for the GM on the standard a SOUND verdict holds a stage to?
why: The fourth rounds found real defects that are NEW, not REPEATED or REVERSING. Field's 188 outline plots is about half of what its own crossing rule gives (about 367), and sink's binary search assumes an ordering that a closed outline does not have. Nothing oscillates and each fix re-owes only one cheap round (about 2 minutes of agent time), so the loop is not the fault. Accept is not open: SC-001 requires SOUND before a budget enters the program target under FR-002, and a ceiling known to be wrong by about 2x must not reach that target. The one class a tool could catch, an index bound with no cell size, is already T07's check. The standard a SOUND verdict holds a stage to is the rubric S1-S7 the GM approved on 2026-10-28, and the verdicts are applying it as written, so this is not a question for him. What has not converged is the way the rewrites are done: four rounds of patching the factor the last verdict named, while the other factors kept the same kind of fault.
what: One more round on field, sink and pond_bank, with each rewrite shaped as follows. (1) Rederive each stage whole from its contract instead of patching the named factor. Every bound states how it works: what orders or indexes the set, the cell size or reach that limits it (taken from the contract, labeled GUESS where the contract labels it so), and the densest case. (2) Where the contract gives no exact figure, take a conservative ceiling with its reason, since a budget is an upper bound and S7 allows slack up to 2. Field adds the step that selects the outline's plots and counts it, and carries the crossing-rule figure (about 367 at 20), not 188. Field also records plots tried against plots, and writes a corridor's reserve as cells rather than 1 a stretch. (3) Sink drops the binary search for a method that works on a closed outline: index cells a pond's width, or the blocked intervals sorted and swept (both named in sink verdict 3). The ditch test moves inside each candidate line, the setback's intervals are sorted and swept, 59.55 rounds up to 60, and 27 points are counted against 28 segments. (4) pond_bank states its index's cell size and its segment lengths, derives the per-cell counts of the crop and brook segments from them, bounds the standing queries at 40 and 80 (not by nothing found at 10 and 20), states the pond's radii at 40 and 80, and counts one look at the crown's 4 cells for both crown and trunk. After that round: a SOUND stage takes its budget. A stage whose only remaining findings are rounding or wording comes back here for accept. A stage that is still UNDERIVED on a material factor comes back here with all five verdicts.

asked: Under the continue on ask:444-T02-water-round-5 (one more round, each stage rederived whole with every bound's mechanism and ceilings): sink came back LOOSE with an exact tighter bound (the corridors: at most twice the segments, 2,467 at 20), now applied - but make budget-set pins only a SOUND verdict, so a LOOSE cannot be pinned without another round; field came back UNDERIVED a fifth time, on a material factor (the corridor index's cell size and the 30 px width, never stated) with three smaller faults; pond_bank UNDERIVED a third time, on a material factor (a packing bound that inferred a side from an area). Each round finds new, real, narrower defects; at this rate a stage that places things takes five or more rounds, and seventeen stages remain. Course for these three, and is the per-stage standard, at this precision, a question for the GM now?
why: The fault is the screen that runs before dispatch, not what the derivations say. The round-5 ruling relied on T07's check to catch an index bound with no cell size, and T07 is on main. The rewrites passed it all the same and came back on exactly that class: field-5 (the corridor index's cell size never stated, and its 30 px width never converted to ft) and pond_bank-3 (a side inferred from an area). The check holds once per derivation, so one outline-index cells row satisfies it while every new index a rewrite adds goes unchecked. This is why rederiving each stage whole did not converge: each rewrite grew new index terms that carried the same gap. The reviewer is also now refining figures inside S7's factor-2 band (the outline plots went 188, then about 367, then 292), so further rounds without the fix spend time below the rubric's resolution. Sink cannot be accepted: make budget-set pins only SOUND, SC-001 requires SOUND, and feature 409's arbiter-accept-as-verdict covers spec and plan reviews, not work-budget derivations. The per-stage standard is not a question for the GM now. It is the S1-S7 rubric he approved, the verdicts apply it as written, and the cost repeats because a tool misses, which this fix repairs. The GM's own words (request.md, 2026-10-28) ask for that kind of repair in the tooling rather than in being careful, and FR-002 puts the program target and its rounds before him anyway. No packing: the 13 ft, 48 ft, 30 px and 38.6 ft figures are contract inputs the count takes as given, and nothing is being fitted to them.
what: In order. (1) Make the tooling fix below, with its test (red with its condition deleted). (2) Re-screen all three derivations with the fixed check before any dispatch. Each index a derivation uses gets its own cells row: field's corridor index (its cell size in ft, the 30 px width converted to ft, and cells written per stretch counted from both) and pond_bank's footprint grid (its densest case from the smallest side of what it actually holds, crowns and wellheads included, never from an area). Any index a rewrite adds carries its row from the moment it is added. (3) Run one work-budget round, MODE BUDGET, on each. Sink's round is a confirming one: the 2N corridor bound (2,467 / 2,757 / 3,054) and verdict-5's three asides (the brook bisected, a gather of 114/132/153; the drain's box tests counted, at most 7; 5 drain points against 6 segments) applied as the verdict wrote them. Field also applies verdict-5's asides: a 48 ft side spans three 38.6 ft cells; the selection includes any outline vertex between two crossings; the outline plots are L x sqrt(1/26^2 + 1/48^2) = 292/421/618; the brook term uses the outline's 11 (3,591/5,036/7,216); 236 brook segments. Pond_bank also applies verdict-3's asides: lanes meeting at junctions bounded, not only parallel lanes; floor(perimeter/30) seats, 33/43/56; and the brook's width, with a trunk near a cell edge tested against the next cell's segments. (4) A SOUND pins its budget with make budget-set. A stage that returns anything else comes back here with all its verdicts, and the next ruling on it weighs whether its findings move its total by more than S7's slack.
tooling_fix: T07's pre-dispatch derivation check (make work-budget-bundle MODE=budget) holds per index rather than per derivation: every index the derivation names must have its own cells row giving its cell size in ft and a densest-case count derived from a side length, never from an area, and every px figure must carry its ft conversion, or the bundle is refused before dispatch. As landed, it accepted field's and pond_bank's round-5 rewrites, which both came back UNDERIVED on exactly this class.
